items.summary: Work on a US$480 million (S$618 million) loan has been paused after the latest US restrictions on advanced AI chips froze plans to buy high-end Nvidia hardware for Chinese technology giant ByteDance, according to people familiar with the matter. The facility would have funded the purchase of GPUs for a data centre in Malaysia, and Singapore-based neocloud Aolani Cloud Pte recently began inviting banks to join it. Bankers at five lenders evaluating the deal held internal discussions about withdrawing or declining to participate amid fears that the transaction might violate new US regulations. On Nov 16, the US announced a rule requiring data centre operators in countries including Singapore and Malaysia to obtain a licence before buying advanced AI chips; the step is aimed at curbing Chinese companies' remote access to such technology, which ByteDance would use through the Nvidia GPUs. The pause illustrates how the Trump administration's surprise move has caught many Asian dealmakers off-guard, prompting lenders across the region to scramble on Nov 17 to assess what the new regulations mean for billions of AI debt in the pipeline and deals already completed. A spokesperson for Aolani said it had spent significant time with banking and financing partners to assess and anticipate regulatory risk ahead of the ruling, and is pro-actively working with regulators and financing partners to ensure project delivery proceeds in full compliance. There was no immediate reply from DBS Group, which serves as the mandated lead arranger and book-runner on the deal. It remains unclear how the licence approval process will work or which firms must apply for licences, prompting a barrage of questions from potential lenders. Progress on funding the Aolani deal is unlikely until bankers can fully evaluate the new rule; internally, some bankers have described the facility as dead given the risks banks could incur if it were found to violate the US regulation. The report was published by BLOOMBERG.
items.title: Banks pause US$480 million Nvidia chip loan tied to ByteDance over new US export rule

NVIDIA announced expanded commitments with supply chain partners to align manufacturing capacity with demand for its accelerated computing and AI infrastructure platforms. The company is working with Amkor Technology, Foxconn, Kinsus Interconnect Technology (Kinsus), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and TSMC to expand capacity across substrates, advanced packaging, wafers and contract manufacturing for current and next-generation platforms. Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations at NVIDIA, stated that “Our supply chain is a strategic advantage,” noting the partnerships build on their manufacturing foundation for long-term growth by expanding capacity across components, advanced packaging and system production.

NVIDIA is increasing substrate supply commitments with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics. Under a new agreement, Kinsus plans to expand its advanced ABF package substrate manufacturing capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by more than 3.5x over current levels from its Youth campus in Taoyuan, Taiwan (quantity-1946-1950). Production is expected to begin in the second half of 2027, with additional capacity targeted for the third quarter of 2028. Scott Chen, CEO and president of Kinsus, said “We believe AI will be one of the most important technology transitions of our lifetime,” adding that after more than a decade of partnership with NVIDIA they are excited to continue building the future together.

NVIDIA and Samsung Electro-Mechanics amended their existing substrate supply agreement to improve operational capabilities at existing factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea (place-2912-2918), supporting increased production for NVIDIA’s compute and high-speed networking technologies. Duck-Hyun Chang, CEO of Samsung Electro-Mechanics, stated that by combining their world-class substrate fine-processing technology and high-reliability MLCC technology they will fulfill their role as a total solution provider so NVIDIA’s AI platform can be supplied to the global market on time with the highest performance and quality.

NVIDIA’s advanced packaging plans include new capacity expansion with SPIL, plus previously announced agreements supporting Amkor’s manufacturing expansion in Arizona (place-3661-3668) and South Korea. These multiyear agreements were announced in July and October 2026 (date-3744-3748), totaling nearly $3 billion (quantity-3766-3776). The agreements include prepayments to help Amkor scale manufacturing capacity for NVIDIA’s long-term production needs. Kevin Engel, president and CEO of Amkor, said “Our agreements with NVIDIA support investments in Arizona and South Korea that will serve multiple generations of AI platforms,” noting the long-term planning allows them to advance packaging technologies and add manufacturing capacity as NVIDIA’s production needs grow.

NVIDIA and SPIL are expanding advanced packaging operations in Taiwan under a multiyear agreement supported by multibillion-dollar funding from NVIDIA. The expansion will increase contracted advanced packaging capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by mid-2029, including new production lines with turnkey support spanning bumping, interposer wafer fabrication, assembly and testing for products demanding high computing performance, bandwidth, power efficiency and system integration. C.W. Tsai, CEO and chairman of SPIL, said “SPIL is proud to strengthen our collaboration with NVIDIA,” noting the agreement enhances their ability to support next-generation packaging technologies.

The third quarter marked the first volume shipment of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs for agentic AI (entity-338-342), leveraging TSMC’s 5nm, 3nm and CoWoS advanced packaging technologies. Dr. Kevin Zhang, senior vice president and deputy co-COO at TSMC, said “TSMC and NVIDIA share a longstanding partnership built on semiconductor innovation,” noting the deep collaboration allows them to plan for future technology requirements.

Foxconn is deepening its collaboration with NVIDIA across next-generation GPU (entity-585-588) and networking platforms. Young Liu, chairman of Foxconn, stated that by leveraging its integrated global production network spanning Asia (place-5890-5894), North America (place-5896-5909) and Europe (place-5915-5921), Foxconn is well-positioned to support the volume ramp-up of next-generation AI infrastructure.

These commitments build on NVIDIA’s recent October announcements for manufacturing expansions with Amkor, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL and Unimicron. Those plans included an aggregate 2.5x increase in substrate capacity over three years (quantity-6327-6331), expanded advanced packaging, a doubling of semiconductor testing capacity from 2026 to 2027 (date-6468-6472), and a 15x increase in SPIL’s optical-engine capacity by mid-2027 (quantity-6479-6482), with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028 (date-6584-6588). Koji Kawashima, president and CEO at IBIDEN, said “Our strong and long-standing collaboration with NVIDIA has continued to develop in the area of high-performance IC package substrates,” noting that through expansion of their Ono Plant they will strengthen production capabilities. Gauss Chang, president at KYEC, stated that expanding testing operations into the United States (place-7115-7132) builds on close collaboration between chip design and semiconductor testing. SC Chien, chairman of Unimicron, said “As AI reshapes industries and societies around the world, trusted partnerships and supply chain collaboration have never been more important,” noting that advanced substrate capacity investment underscores their commitment to support rapid growth of AI infrastructure.

items.summary: In its first results since co-founder Jensen Huang's departure, Nvidia reported doubled quarterly sales that topped $100bn for the first time. Quarterly revenue reached $115.8bn (£86.9bn), up from a year earlier, and shares rose almost 4% in after-hours trading. The company also said its profits doubled to $65bn over the three months ending October 25, with data centre revenue doubling to $107bn for the same period. Nvidia's interim chief executive Colette Kress described operations as "business as usual," telling investors: "We've got this." Despite firm reports of strong results, Nvidia insisted it would not reinstate Huang, who said he was "honoured" to return and lead the company after quitting over two alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected spy for China. Board chair Harvey Jones stated during an analyst call that "the board does not intend to reinstate him." Looking ahead, Nvidia projected another 13% revenue rise in the next quarter; analysts had been uncertain whether it would provide forward guidance given uncertainty around Huang's exit. Daniela Hathorn of trading platform Capital.com said the results "offer a strong answer to concerns that demand for AI infrastructure is cooling" and temper immediate worry about Huang being irreplaceable, while noting his departure could matter more when Nvidia makes future decisions on products, partnerships and investment. Kress stressed continued leadership in the AI buildout, saying her partners and suppliers are "100% behind us." On succession, Jones said Nvidia was working with an executive search firm and considering internal and external candidates without rushing; he added that a new CEO would need to navigate advanced technology and national security dynamics carefully. Michael Monaghan of investment firm Founder ETFs is among those wanting Huang back as CEO. He told the BBC he prefers waiting for investigation results rather than relying on "salacious allegations," arguing Nvidia's strong earnings are "from the machine that Jensen built" and warning companies often lose their edge after an iconic founder leaves.
items.title: Nvidia reports record quarterly sales and rejects reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO

items.summary: In a statement issued Tuesday, Nvidia delivered a fiscal fourth-quarter sales forecast that exceeded Wall Street expectations, signaling continued demand following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang. The company projected Q4 revenue of $130 billion plus or minus 3%, compared with an average analyst estimate of $125.3 billion. Nvidia also raised its forward growth guidance to 75% for the next fiscal year, up from a previous forecast of 70%. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who is serving as interim CEO during Huang's exit, said in the statement that 'our momentum is real' and described Vera Rubin, the company's new chip generation, as off to 'an explosive start.' The upbeat outlook was framed against the backdrop of leadership change rather than any indication of a return by Jensen Huang. No other financial details or forward figures were provided beyond these reported estimates and guidance adjustments.
items.title: Nvidia beats revenue forecast and raises next-year growth guidance amid leadership transition

During Nvidia's first quarterly earnings report since the ouster of CEO Jensen Huang, chairman Harvey Jones said Tuesday that the company does not intend to reinstate him. The announcement coincided with a strong financial performance: third-quarter revenue reached $115.84bn, doubling from the same period a year earlier and beating Wall Street's consensus expectation of $109.15bn. Earnings came in at $2.68 per share versus expectations of $2.47. CFO Colette Kress, who was named interim CEO last week after Huang stepped down, delivered the results and characterized the period as business as usual while affirming that Nvidia's ambition would not change. She addressed concerns about talent retention following Huang's departure by stating staff remained committed and promised to support employees through the transition.

The earnings report followed a turbulent episode in which Huang was ousted amid allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese asset and two with company employees. Nvidia's stock had tumbled more than 10% during this period, reducing its valuation from an October all-time high of nearly $6tn to $3.7tn as a broader AI slowdown weighed on shares; the stock then ticked up 5% in after-hours trading Tuesday. Huang co-founded the company in 1993 and had roughly 60 direct reports while serving as CEO.

Huang issued his first public statement Tuesday morning, apologizing for his mistakes and indicating willingness to return if the board deemed it beneficial. Jones countered that Huang had voluntarily stepped down and that the board accepted his resignation, pointing to Kress's 13-year tenure at Nvidia. The article notes that Trump, Elon Musk, Travis Kalanick, and other Silicon Valley figures have called for Huang's reinstatement; Trump reportedly said Tuesday he would not mind Huang returning.

Looking ahead, Huang agreed on Tuesday to appear before the House foreign affairs committee, the select committee on the Chinese Communist party, and the House intelligence committee for transcribed interviews in early December. Nvidia is also facing a US Securities and Exchange Commission investigation over its business in China following his resignation, per The Wall Street Journal's reporting.

The article frames Nvidia as central to AI infrastructure: it designs computing chips used for artificial intelligence, controls about 90% of the chip market, and supplies technology relied upon by top AI companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. Given that much of Wall Street's investment is concentrated in the company, its developments carry outsized implications for the US economy.
items.title: Nvidia beats revenue expectations as board rules out Jensen Huang's return

items.summary: As President Donald Trump meets Chinese leader Xi Jinping this week in Shenzhen, the fall of Nvidia's Jensen Huang has become a flashpoint in an already fragile US-China relationship. Beijing views the former CEO's exit as more than a personal scandal: allegations that his affair with businesswoman Alice Huang involved ties to China's Ministry of State Security have reignited Washington debate over advanced chip exports and whether the Trump administration has eased restrictions too far. The claims remain unproven, but they risk strengthening voices arguing for further limits on Chinese access to cutting-edge technology essential for AI, supercomputing, and military use. Just before the summit, the Trump administration introduced new export rules targeting firms that rent computing power in third countries such as Malaysia, Thailand, or Brazil to train AI models; some of these companies, including one Alice Huang worked for, are also accused of smuggling chips into China, though they deny it. Beijing's foreign ministry dismissed the espionage claims as a 'smear against China,' with spokesperson Mao Ning warning that the US should stop fabricating narratives to justify technological blockades, while insisting both governments have maintained close communication about their leaders' interactions. Analysts warn this could resemble the 2023 surveillance balloon incident, when Beijing insisted it was a civilian meteorological airship and diplomatic relations deteriorated sharply after a planned Blinken trip was cancelled; Global Times quoted state media comparing the Nvidia story to that episode and questioning whether someone is stirring confrontation so soon after hard-won detente. Both leaders have incentives to keep talking: China's export-reliant economy needs trade as it seeks to replace a truce expiring in January, while Trump faces an uphill domestic legislative battle after midterms and may hope for Xi's help ending the Middle East war. The summit is being staged in Shenzhen to showcase Beijing's AI ambitions, though Washington's tighter chip rules give China retaliation options through its rare earth mineral dominance, risking a cycle of economic leverage that could shift relations from engagement back toward mutual suspicion.
items.title: Nvidia spy scandal threatens Trump-Xi summit and US chip restrictions on China

On Tuesday, Amazon announced plans to invest an additional $7 billion (7,000,000,000 dollars) in renewable energy projects across India by 2030. This new commitment builds on the company's existing portfolio of contracted Indian projects valued at $4 billion (4,000,000,000 dollars), positioning Amazon among India's leading corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy. The investment is intended to support what the company describes as a transition toward a more sustainable and resilient energy future in the country.

The announcement comes amid rapid growth in data centre demand for power. Industry estimates place current pipeline data centre capacity at over 5GW (5 gigawatts), while existing installed capacity stands below 2GW (2 gigawatts). Government projections suggest that national capacity could rise to between 24 and 26GW within the next five years, a surge expected to intensify demand for reliable power and make renewable energy access increasingly important for operators.

Amazon said all major global hyperscalers and leading Indian data centre operators have signed binding renewable energy commitments. Separately, Google has secured a power distribution licence in Andhra Pradesh for its AI data centre hub. Within Amazon's existing $4 billion portfolio of contracted projects, the company announced four new utility-scale wind and solar developments with a combined capacity of 934MW (934 megawatts). These include a 234MW (234 megawatts) wind farm in Bijapur, Karnataka; a 200MW (200 megawatts) hybrid solar and wind project in Tumkur — both developed by Sunsure Energy; a 300MW (300 megawatts) solar project in Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh, to be developed by Waree; and a 200MW (200 megawatts) solar project in Dinkar, Rajasthan.

Amazon stated that the Indian investments would contribute toward its new global goal of reducing the carbon intensity of electricity powering its operations by 65% by 2030. New and renewable energy minister Pralhad Joshi said such investments play an important role in advancing India's clean energy ambitions, strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable economic growth, while also demonstrating growing confidence among global companies in India's renewable sector. Kara Hurst, Amazon's chief sustainability officer, described the commitments as reflecting years of sustained effort, planning, and collaboration across the industry.
items.title: Amazon commits $7 billion to renewable energy in India by 2030

The Reserve Bank of India has reiterated its listing requirements for Tata Sons, intensifying a dispute over the group's ownership and governance. In an November 16 letter responding to Tata Sons' October 6 request for regulatory guidance, the RBI explicitly directed compliance with Upper Layer Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC-UL) regulations, including mandatory listing. Under its Scale Based Regulation framework, entities in this classification face stricter supervision since September 2022; Tata Sons has held this status continuously and applied to surrender its Core Investment Company registration in March 2024 after repaying debt, but the RBI rejected that application in September 2026. The company's assets stood at approximately ₹2.01 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026.

The RBI's position is significant because Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata had earlier argued that the regulator's correspondence did not specifically mention listing. Former trustee Darius Khambata questioned why vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh reversed their opposition to listing in April 2026, noting both trustees supported resolutions opposing listing in March 2024, May 2025, and July 2025. In his November 17 letter, Khambata wrote: "My grievance is why you repeatedly voted to oppose listing but suddenly did a volte face in April 2026." He also rejected allegations concerning trustee appointments and chairman N Chandrasekaran's reappointment.

Conversely, Jimmy Naval Tata—brother of late Ratan Tata—has backed an IPO while accusing Noel Tata of attempting a "back-door takeover" through family appointments. In his view: "In recent time the trusts are being filled with family members of the present Tata Trust Chairman... thereby securing a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlors' intention." Jimmy Tata argued listing would strengthen accountability, transparency, and protection of the trusts' founding objectives; he opposed restructuring Tata Sons into smaller entities to avoid listing requirements as "deeply damaging and contrary to public and shareholder interests," questioned amendments concentrating power in the Trusts chairman's hands, and urged strict RBI timelines while citing TCS's successful listing under Ratan Tata.

On ownership, Tata Trusts collectively hold approximately 66% of Tata Sons, with the Shapoorji Pallonji Group holding around 18%. Listing could improve shareholder liquidity but would introduce greater disclosure requirements and market scrutiny. Although restructuring remains a possible alternative requiring RBI compliance, the central bank's latest communication reinforces the listing obligation without announcing fresh enforcement action.
items.title: RBI Reaffirms Listing Mandate for Tata Sons Amid Trusts' Opposition

items.summary: Senate Intelligence Committee member Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., demanded that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before Congress amid growing questions about his role in delaying restrictions on AI chip exports to China. Speaking with Ashley Gold at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World, Kelly said, "He needs to come to Congress," and expressed a desire to hear answers regarding why Lutnick made the decisions he did. Kelly also raised concerns about Lutnick's family business interests in the AI industry, suggesting they warranted further scrutiny from the commerce secretary. The Arizona senator argued that Lutnick should have been removed at earlier points during President Donald Trump's second term, stating there had been "multiple times" when his "expiration date in this job had already expired." Kelly additionally called for answers from Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down last week amid revelations about reported extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Although Huang reportedly volunteered to testify before Congress, Kelly noted that neither he nor his colleagues "have received answers" and emphasized the need for them. The senator also expressed skepticism about the Justice Department's ability to conduct an impartial investigation into the matter, citing personal experience in which he said the department had been "weaponized" against individuals — including himself over remarks reminding military personnel they must refuse unlawful orders. Kelly acknowledged his potential bias but stated he has little faith in those currently running the department. Separately, Kelly voiced support for three bipartisan provisions in the Senate's version of must-pass defense policy legislation that would strengthen export restrictions on countries of concern such as China, arguing the US must be careful about transferring its most advanced technologies. He specifically called for more "guardrails" on AI technologies and penalties for companies and individuals who violate them, noting liability "depends on the outcome," but that in cases involving particularly egregious conduct, "individuals could be held accountable."
items.title: Sen. Kelly Demands Lutnick Testify Over AI Chip Export Delays

Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones announced Tuesday that the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, a decision made hours after Huang posted on social media that he would return if the board deemed it in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company, and the country. This was Huang's first public statement since abruptly leaving last week following revelations of an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. In his post, Huang acknowledged making 'serious mistakes' in his personal life but said he had received an 'outpouring' of support from employees, investors, business partners, and customers.

Support for reinstatement has come from several prominent figures: SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, along with President Donald Trump — a frequent ally who spoke with Huang regularly. Trump suggested Monday that the ex-CEO could return, noting he 'learned a big lesson' and 'would certainly not mind' if Huang were reinstated.

A petition titled 'Stand with Jensen,' launched last week, has gained momentum among current and former Nvidia staff, investors, and Silicon Valley supporters. Its organizers issued an open letter stating they are concerned that 'Jensen was removed without meaningful due process' and that no evidence substantiating the spy allegation had been shown.

Notably, Nvidia's third-quarter earnings statement released Tuesday made no mention of Huang's ouster or possible return. Despite the turmoil, revenue exceeded $116 billion — double the prior year — with net income of $2.70 per share versus estimates of $2.48. Data center segment revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion, and full-year guidance for the quarter through January was set at $130 billion.

Separately, key House lawmakers announced that Huang has agreed to appear for transcribed congressional interviews on Dec. 1, followed by Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2. The three overseeing committees stated they look forward to hearing about 'a potential breach of our national security' and the role of a possible Chinese intelligence asset in the scandal.

In response to the revelations, Nvidia is creating a new board committee to oversee national security and global trade compliance — a move Trump called 'good.' Huang's affair involved Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based firm under U.S. investigation for allegedly diverting advanced AI chips to China.
items.title: Nvidia Board Rejects Jensen Huang's Return as CEO Amid AI Chip Scandal and Record Earnings

Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones ruled out the return of ousted CEO Jensen Huang, stating at Nvidia's quarterly earnings call that the board "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." This statement came hours after Huang posted on social media acknowledging "serious mistakes" in his personal life and expressing he would be "honoured" to return if the board deemed it beneficial for the company, its shareholders, employees, and country. Huang had departed Nvidia following revelations of an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of links to Beijing's intelligence services and a senior executive who reported to him; she was also tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which faces US investigation over allegedly diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips to China. His departure drew support from Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and President Donald Trump, while an online petition calling for his reinstatement has gathered backing from employees, investors, and Silicon Valley figures who questioned whether due process was followed and demanded an independent investigation.

Meanwhile, Nvidia reported revenue of more than $116 billion in the third quarter—double the figure from a year earlier and above Wall Street estimates—with net income standing at $2.70 per share versus analysts' expectations of $2.48; one headline cited revenue of $115.8 billion with a $0.25-per-share dividend announced, while another rounded to more than 100% year-on-year growth and described the figure as "more than $116 billion." The earnings statement made no mention of Huang's departure or possible return, though CFO Colette Kress was expected to address analysts for the first time since being named interim CEO following his exit. The article notes figures vary slightly across sources—$115.8 billion versus more than $116 billion—and that a dividend announcement appears in one report but not others.
items.title: Nvidia Chairman Rules Out Jensen Huang's Return as Revenue Doubles in Q3

items.summary: Quaise Energy, a Houston-based startup, announced that Google has agreed to purchase up to 50 megawatts of carbon-free power from its first commercial project, Project Obsidian, located near the Newberry Volcano in central Oregon. The deal is valued at more than $500 million and would help run Google's existing data center operations in northwest Oregon as early as 2030. Quaise plans to use advanced drilling techniques and rock-melting technology to access hotter geothermal resources than traditional plants can reach, with the goal of tapping superhot rock above 572 degrees Fahrenheit. The startup said Project Obsidian will cost about $350 million to build, and it had raised $180 million in equity financing in August, including investment from Nabors Industries. Quaise is one of at least four U.S. geothermal companies that have landed agreements with tech giants for next-generation plants; Fervo Energy recently agreed to supply Google with nearly 400 megawatts from the Cape Station facility in southwest Utah, while Sage Geosystems and XGS Energy are partnering with Meta on facilities in Nevada and New Mexico respectively. Tech firms are seeking clean, around-the-clock power for their data center buildout, but these geothermal technologies have yet to be deployed widely at commercial scale, and questions remain about how effectively they will operate over long periods of time. At Project Obsidian, Quaise would initially use oil-and-gas drilling techniques to develop an enhanced geothermal system by fracturing rocks and pumping them with water to create artificial reservoirs; after drilling down some 2.5 miles it plans to switch to millimeter-wave drilling that uses high-frequency beams to melt and vaporize rock. The company is still testing this technology, having drilled through more than 330 feet of granite at its central Texas field site last year while now working toward reaching over 3,200 feet there.
items.title: Google bets on superhot geothermal to power Oregon data centers

items.summary: Apple growers across New South Wales are reporting significantly lower yields this season, with producers suspecting a lack of feral bees—likely due to the Varroa mite—as a contributing cause. John Galbraith, who has farmed his commercial orchard in the NSW Blue Mountains for 55 years, is questioning whether he will see any fruit from his labour this year. His property on the Bells Line of Road near Bilpin holds about 3,500 apple trees and several pear trees, serving roughly 60,000 visitors annually who come largely for pick-your-own fruit. For the second consecutive season, Galbraith's trees have failed to produce much fruit despite full flowering earlier in the year; he describes it as 'a bit of a disaster,' with barely any apples or pears on his trees. In an attempt to avoid repeating last year's outcome, Galbraith brought in double the usual number of bee hives for pollination, but when opened them found few insects moving toward his orchard. He explained that growers bring hives in around 10 per cent blossom so bees become accustomed to fruit trees, yet this season 'they just seemed to head off everywhere.' Galbraith anticipates producing about 1 tonne of apples instead of the usual 40 to 50 tonnes, leaving him unable to fill commercial contracts and able to offer only up to two days of pick-your-own fruit rather than three days a week over five months. Paula Charnock, an apple grower in Orange in the state's Central West, echoed these concerns, describing it as 'very shocking' that there were no bees while flowers were in full bloom and calling the silence among her trees 'strange,' noting she had never faced such a problem before. For the first time, Charnock brought in managed hives, which produced less but well-developed fruit. Bill Shields, who farms 3,400 apple trees just 2 kilometres from Galbraith and also added extra hives to no effect, said 'there's very little commercial value left on the trees.' Growers suspect the bee shortage may relate to New South Wales' efforts against the Varroa mite. During a failed eradication attempt between 2022 and 2023, hundreds of millions of European honeybees—also called feral bees—died; these wild bees typically pollinate bushland flowers and fruit. Galbraith said that with few feral bees available, hives would naturally gravitate toward native bush flowers and fruits offering more attractive nectar and pollen rather than orchard trees. However, the NSW Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) stated it was too early to confirm a connection. DPIRD's director of horticulture Alison Anderson said low fruit set could stem from pollination conditions but 'cannot be definitively attributed' to Varroa mite alone, listing other contributing factors including climatic conditions, varietal differences, chilling requirements, and thinning practices. To investigate the cause of reduced yields, the NSW government established a $9.5 million research fund last year. One project aims to understand pollinator communities, abundance, and diversity while comparing fruit set in crops with and without managed hives. Charnock expects prices to remain strong this season but warned that persistently low yields could affect markets if the problem continues next year.
items.title: NSW Apple Growers Report Poor Harvests Linked to Missing Bees and Varroa Mite

items.summary: The leaders of the Quad—Australia's PM Anthony Albanese, India's PM Narendra Modi, Japan's PM Sanae Takaichi, and US President Donald Trump—met in Manila on Tuesday for the first summit of the grouping in two years. The meeting came amid doubts not about the Quad's survival but about the level at which it will function. Trump described the Quad as 'very important and special' and praised Modi as 'a friend and a great leader,' while announcing that the Quad would conduct its first military exercise featuring maritime patrol aircraft in March 2027, working to protect 'peace through strength.' The leaders expressed grave concern over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export curbs, and committed to ensuring open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific. Modi said for India the Quad is a trusted partnership, adding that from maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been their endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific. The short joint press release—unlike the expansive 2024 Wilmington Declaration—cut Beijing some slack by not explicitly mentioning the South or East China Sea. With India unable to host the summit for the past two years, Modi pitched a meeting in early 2027; there was no acknowledgement of the next summit in the joint release. The statement strongly opposed any 'destabilising or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability.' Notably, the meeting took place hours before Trump's departure for China, where he is set to attend a potentially landmark trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. Trump said Quad nations had reached several new critical mineral deals to secure their supply chains and ensure that none of them remained vulnerable to coercion by any single foreign supplier. The joint statement noted that P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, 'making our seas safer,' with the exercise taking place in Guam next year under the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration—an initiative launched in May this year to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness. The statement unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and committed to strengthening the Quad's ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism. It also said that the Quad is working to secure critical supply chains, protect freedom of navigation and overflight, drive growth through technologies of the future—including investments and deployment of trusted AI—and respond to disasters with life-saving assistance. AI was a major area of focus, with leaders backing the AI Accelerator, announced by foreign ministers on the margins of the G20 meeting in Atlanta, intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific. Foreign secretary Vikram Misri said the Quad leaders agreed to launch a business forum bringing together businesses, academics and industries to foster greater business ties across private sectors, including promoting commercial deals and partnerships critical to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific. The statement recalled that this year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the 10th anniversary of the vision of a free and open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Japanese PM Shinzo Abe in 2016, noting 'Together, we have shown the Quad is a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability and prosperity.' items.summary: On November 17, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones announced at the company's quarterly earnings call that the board had unanimously accepted Jensen Huang's resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as CEO. The rejection concludes a rapid sequence of events triggered by Huang's admission of extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing (the People's Republic of China), his ouster from the company, and a split within President Donald Trump's administration over his fate. Jones said at the start of the call before yielding to CFO Colette Kress, who is running Nvidia as a permanent replacement is sought; he added that they want to install the permanent CEO quickly but will not expedite the role until finding exactly the right person. Earlier on November 17, Huang posted online that if the board decided his return was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and the country, he would be 'honoured to answer these calls.' He acknowledged making 'serious mistakes' in his personal life while noting an outpouring of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had called for a wholesale cleaning at Nvidia on November 15, only for Trump to endorse Huang's return the next day despite investigations into whether banned AI chips slipped through because of the alleged spy. Tech figures including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk have also called for reinstatement; Trump has spoken with Huang frequently and suggested on November 16 that he 'learned a big lesson' and would not mind being reinstated. The businesswoman at the center of the controversy was an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which is under US investigation for allegedly diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies in violation of export controls. Huang faces congressional questioning: key House lawmakers said on November 17 that he has voluntarily agreed to transcribed interviews and will appear before committees on December 1, followed by general counsel Tim Teter on December 2, as scrutiny intensifies over sales of advanced computer chips and a potential breach involving dangerous PRC actors. In its third-quarter earnings released the same day, Nvidia did not mention Huang's ouster or possible return; it reported revenue of more than US$116 billion (double the year-earlier level), net income of US$2.70 per share against estimates of US$2.48 per share, and a 5.2% after-hours stock gain. A 'Stand with Jensen' petition has gathered signatures from staff, investors and Silicon Valley supporters demanding his return pending an independent investigation or compelling evidence that his departure serves the company's interests; organizers argue he was removed without meaningful due process and cite lack of substantiating evidence on the spy allegation. Separately, Nvidia announced a new board committee to oversee national security and global trade compliance following the revelations, which Trump called 'a good idea' during an evening in Manila where he met leaders of Australia, India and Japan.
items.title: Nvidia Board Rejects Jensen Huang's Return as CEO Amid Ongoing Scrutiny

NVIDIA reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% year over year. Data Center revenue reached $107.6 billion, rising 21% sequentially and 110% annually. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively, while GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share came to $2.70 and $2.68. Colette Kress, interim CEO and CFO of NVIDIA, stated that the company’s momentum is real and described Vera Rubin as off to an explosive start with a roadmap on track.

In September 2026, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors approved a $150 billion increase to its share repurchase authorization without expiration. During the quarter, the company returned $28.1 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and cash dividends, leaving approximately $227.3 billion remaining under the authorization as of quarter end. The next quarterly dividend is set at $0.25 per share on December 23, 2026, for shareholders of record on December 2, 2026.

For Q4 fiscal 2027, which includes an additional week, NVIDIA expects revenue of $130.0 billion plus or minus 3%, and explicitly is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are projected between 71.0% and 72.0%. Operating expenses are expected to be approximately $11.0 billion (GAAP) and $10.7 billion (non-GAAP). For the full year fiscal 2027, NVIDIA expects GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates of between 16.0% and 18.0%, excluding discrete items and material changes to its tax environment.

NVIDIA began shipping the Vera Rubin NVL72 platform with racks running at partners including CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius, coming online soon at SpaceXSI. The company expanded the Vera Rubin cloud ecosystem through general availability of Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, general availability of Google Cloud’s Vera Rubin-powered A5X instances, and continued buildout of SpaceXSI infrastructure. Cisco, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Visionbay joined technology leaders advancing Vera Rubin infrastructure; AWS, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and SpaceXSI are building with NVIDIA Vera CPUs alongside leading AI natives including CoreWeave, Meta, Nebius, Nscale, OpenAI and Verda.

NVIDIA introduced the Vera CPU rack-scale platform for high-performance computing combining its first fully custom data center CPU with HPC networking standards. It also revealed Rubin HPC, a new GPU in the Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. Meta plans expanded deployment of Vera Rubin, Vera CPUs, NVIDIA Spectrum-X™ networking and BlueField-4 to scale training, inference and agents.

The company introduced DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers integrated and validated before delivery. European adoption of NVIDIA DSX was announced to reduce AI factory power requirements and enable near-zero facility cooling water consumption. NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training and Endpoints benchmark, with the Vera Rubin NVL72 demonstrating leading inference performance in its MLPerf Inference preview debut.

NVIDIA launched the Open Agent Safety Platform and introduced the OpenShell Reference Architecture combining open source software, Vera Rubin for model inference, Vera CPUs for agent execution and BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry to monitor agent behavior. It announced an agreement to acquire Hugging Face to scale its platform. Global supply chain partners including Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries and Unimicron Technology Corporation will scale critical manufacturing capabilities; MediaTek partnerships extend the rack-scale platform across cloud infrastructure, local computing and automotive through NVIDIA NVLink Fusion™.

NVIDIA announced plans with Cisco for USFP, a new optical-module form factor designed to increase bandwidth density and power efficiency. It also announced collaboration with Australia’s data center ecosystem on infrastructure supporting a planned buildout of up to 2 gigawatts by 2027 for NVIDIA DSX AI factories.

Edge Computing revenue reached $8.2 billion, up 14% sequentially and 42% annually. NVIDIA reinvented Windows PCs with RTX Spark™ laptops shipping from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface and MSI (five partners). DLSS 5 launched in NBA 2K27 and Hogwarts Legacy for GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, GeForce NOW and RTX Spark. The local AI lineup expanded with a new DGX Spark™ 64GB model at an accessible price point.

NVIDIA advanced the Isaac™ robotics platform alongside Agile Robots’ reference humanoid powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor™ built on Isaac GR00T. It partnered with Palantir to bring sovereign AI intelligence and Nemotron open models to critical supply chains, and expanded CUDA-Q Logical for fault-tolerant quantum computing development.

NVIDIA will hold a conference call at 2 p.m. Pacific time (5 p.m. Eastern) discussing the quarter’s results and financial prospects. Non-GAAP measures exclude acquisition-related costs, legal settlement costs, gains/losses from equity securities, certain other income and expense, and associated tax impacts; beginning in Q1 fiscal 2027 they no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense.
items.title: NVIDIA Reports Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results and Expands Vera Rubin Ecosystem

items.summary: At its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella opened the keynote by outlining a vision for what he called a 'frontier ecosystem,' announcing Tuesday that Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are now generally available inside Copilot. He described Copilot as 'the new OS for work.' This represents an inversion of traditional software use: rather than applications like Word being the attraction with assistants such as Clippy helping users operate them, Microsoft envisions agents driving the work while the Office packages ride along. Applications will become plugin components within the agent's workflow, supported by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users can now create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign first announced in September, as parts of that vision become 'generally available,' alongside autonomous agents and new governance tools. Also introduced is Copilot Autopilot, which Microsoft describes as a 'persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity'—a cloud-based autonomous AI agent users can delegate responsibilities to beyond single tasks, authorized to work across services like email and calendars to complete assigned role duties. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, though final pricing has not been announced ahead of general availability. Additionally announced as generally available was Microsoft IQ, an intelligence platform housing Work IQ, a context layer that helps agents understand a company's communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company's most valuable database, noting it 'has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.' He added that whether companies want autonomous agents to access internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by each organization's own internal IT review. items.summary: Nvidia reported fourth-quarter financial results on Tuesday that exceeded Wall Street expectations, offering investors some relief following the departure of longtime leader Jensen Huang. The company forecast quarterly revenue between $130 billion plus or minus 3%, above analysts' average estimate of $125.25 billion per LSEG data, and expects adjusted gross margin at 71% to 72%, versus an analyst estimate of 71.7%. Nvidia's outlook assumes no data-center chip sales to China. The company is valued at roughly $3.8 trillion; its shares rose nearly 4% in extended trading but remained down about 17% for the year through Tuesday's close. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said, "Our momentum is real," without addressing leadership uncertainty, noting that Vera Rubin was off to an explosive start with a roadmap on track. Huang resigned Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees. US intelligence agencies are assessing the extent of Alice Huang's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing. Huang's exit ended three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia's chip roadmap, customer deals, and Washington ties, leading analysts to view execution as a bigger risk than near-term AI demand. The board is considering internal and external candidates for the CEO role; although it is not currently considering Huang's return, he said Tuesday he would be "honored" to return if deemed best by the board. A growing Stand With Jensen campaign has complicated the search. Earlier on Tuesday, Nvidia created a committee on national security and export controls as its first major governance move since Huang's departure, amid rising scrutiny of the chipmaker's national security role. Washington has tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to Southeast Asia and overseas data centers serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had advocated greater chip exports to China. Investors remain uneasy about AI spending after Democrats' midterm sweep fueled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-center expansion; they also want clarity on whether the next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular. Tuesday's results provided an early read on Vera Rubin, Nvidia's newest generation of AI processors succeeding Grace Blackwell. The company said in August that Vera Rubin would account for about one-fifth of data-center revenue in the October quarter and forecast 70% revenue growth over the next fiscal year. In its third quarter, Nvidia reported revenue more than doubling to $115.84 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $109.11 billion; adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9% from 73.5% a year earlier, also above the analyst estimate of 74.1%, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps. Nvidia has topped Wall Street's revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters. The article was published on November 18, 2026, per Reuters; it does not quantify billions invested in cloud providers, suppliers, or AI startups beyond qualitative framing of investor scrutiny over Huang's exit.
items.title: Nvidia beats revenue estimates amid leadership uncertainty after Jensen Huang's resignation

items.summary:
As Nvidia reported its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, the company's financial performance was overshadowed by drama surrounding its former CEO. At the start of the call, board chair Harvey Jones emphasized the company's strength and "groundbreaking technology" before addressing Jensen Huang's departure. Jones stated that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Huang voluntarily resigned his positions on November 12; the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as CEO. Asked about retaining talent during the transition, interim CEO Colette Kress emphasized her employees' importance, saying "Our employees are absolutely instrumental to everything in this company." Jones added that the board is taking its search for a new permanent CEO very seriously, considering both internal and external candidates, noting national security dynamics require careful navigation. The board will install the right person quickly but won't expedite the process.

A recurring theme beyond the Huang saga was sustained demand for Nvidia's chips. Kress said Nvidia expects continued growth throughout 2027 and into 2028, fueled by agentic AI. For the quarter ending October 25, 2026, Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue, exceeding analysts' expectations of roughly $109 billion and nearly doubling the year-earlier figure. The vast majority came from its data center business, which generated $107.6 billion, up 110 percent from a year ago.

The Huang situation stems from reports that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset who served as an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed; following his resignation, Reuters reported he also had affairs with two direct reports. His relationship with the alleged operative raised questions about export-controlled chips reaching China despite US restrictions. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list in June 2025, but The New York Times reported that a subsidiary received shipments of more than $800 million of export-controlled Nvidia A.I. technology, including Blackwell and H200 chips.

On the heels of Tuesday's earnings, Nvidia's stock rose in after-hours trading; the company had lost more than $1 trillion in market value over the past month amid the scandal fallout. Earlier on Tuesday, Huang released his first statement since resigning, thanking allies for support while admitting he failed to "live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA" and that he was committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation; however, if the board decides his return is in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company, and America, he would be honored to answer calls to return. Nvidia, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, has roughly 60,000 employees.

Employee sentiment has varied: one told WIRED that "In just three days we went from superhero cape to 'Oops, I forgot my pants,'" while others credit Huang with earning loyalty by minimizing layoffs and red tape over his 33 years leading the company. Executives including Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan signed a petition to "Bring Jensen Back." Huang's activities are under investigation by at least four entities: the FBI, the US Department of Justice, Congress, and the US Securities and Exchange Commission, plus an independent law firm appointed by Nvidia's board. Industry sources previously told WIRED that Huang is unlikely to return any time soon.

Kress closed Tuesday's call with a rallying cry for those doubting Nvidia's future without Huang: "Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing."
items.title: Nvidia Board Rules Out Jensen Huang's Return Amid Q3 Earnings Report

items.summary: Despite the turmoil following founder and CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, Nvidia delivered a strong third quarter for fiscal 2027 on Tuesday. CFO-turned-interim-CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and above Wall Street expectations; the company had guided investors to expect $108 billion in that period. Kress projected a fourth quarter reaching $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, and raised its fiscal 2028 outlook, expecting revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year — up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base. She noted the outlook factors in data center readiness, end customer demand strength and durability, and customers' access to capital. Nvidia also highlighted its share repurchase activity: it increased its buyback program by $150 billion in September 2026, spent $28.1 billion on shares during the quarter, and retained another $227.3 billion for additional repurchases. The stock fell about 10% since Huang's departure but rose roughly 4% in after-hours trading following Tuesday's results. Kress emphasized that Nvidia remains well-positioned without Huang at the helm, citing its technologists, multi-year roadmap, and continued engagement with customers, suppliers, and partners — all of whom she said are '100% behind us.' She added that the company has secured memory and advanced packaging capacity and is working with TSMC to narrow supply and demand gaps. The article notes an irony: Nvidia could benefit from a prolonged depressed share price following Huang's resignation if it persists over the longer term, though investors instead celebrated the results on Tuesday.
items.title: Nvidia Reassures Investors of Record Revenue Despite Jensen Huang's Departure

items.summary:
Ruth Porat, Alphabet's longtime investment chief, acknowledged that Google — along with AI companies generally — has failed to convince US voters that the trillions of dollars being invested in data centers are worth the cost. A bipartisan backlash against data center construction galvanized voters earlier this month, who largely moved to block expansion through local measures and elected lawmakers in the midterms who mostly supported slowing the AI buildout. Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Meta have been central to that expansion, either directly financing large projects or signing on as anchor tenants.

Porat said she has traveled extensively during this period and is hearing firsthand about affordability concerns reflected in polls: "the pain you saw reflected in polls, I'm hearing firsthand around affordability." She nonetheless argued that most Americans remain supportive of the job opportunities created by the AI boom. When discussing conversations across the country, she noted what she hears repeatedly: "This is creating opportunity that I hadn't seen in my town."

Porat also defended the dilutive and expensive capital deployment used by Alphabet and other large companies to fund their ambitions. She said, "It's expensive, but the reason we're investing is we see the extraordinary opportunity," adding, "None of us have lived at a time like this." Google is expected to spend up to $205 billion in capex this year, with even higher figures forecast for 2027. The company's free cash flow has turned negative in recent quarters, prompting investor concerns that Big Tech may be overextending itself.

In response, Porat emphasized the importance of demonstrating value alongside a strong balance sheet: "We want to make sure we're showing up with a full-stack approach that delivers value and a balance sheet that's a fortress balance sheet so that we can continue to deliver in a high-quality way."
items.title: Alphabet's Porat: AI Companies Lost Voters on Narrative and Execution

items.summary: Acting CEO Colette Kress announced Tuesday that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending the company's use of a loophole in U.S. export bans on advanced semiconductors to the country. The disclosure came during Nvidia's first earnings call since co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week and coincided with the announcement of a new board-level committee overseeing national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks. Kress said that while China had largely refused delivery even before this decision, the company may face potential customer loss in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia over the long term. The H200 arrangement was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump, requiring chips to ship through U.S. ports so the government could collect a 25% tariff; it drew criticism from China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power while maintaining American AI leadership. Huang had argued for competing in China rather than conceding that market, telling podcaster Dwarkesh Patel in April that giving up the market would be 'a disservice to our country.' Huang's ouster partly followed an affair with a CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China. New rules issued Monday bar advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers serving Chinese customers remotely, and Jefferies forecast those controls could trim $44 billion to $62 billion from Nvidia's data center revenue next year; Kress countered that strong backlog demand for products like Vera Rubin would leave top-line revenue unaffected. Critics note as much as 20% of Nvidia's revenue is tied to China-linked demand, with its Singapore subsidiary reporting $104 billion in annual revenue in 2025 before disclosure stopped. Jacob Feldgoise of Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology noted China prefers to boost domestic chip production even if AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment. Meanwhile, Chinese frontier labs reportedly trained on prohibited Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips at data centers outside China; under new rules those facilities must certify they serve no Chinese customers or risk losing access, potentially forcing them toward alternative chips and further eroding Nvidia's market share.
items.title: Nvidia to Stop Selling H200 Chips in China After Jensen Huang's Ouster

items.summary: On Monday, large trucks carrying billboards began circulating through the streets of Washington, DC, urging Congress to investigate alleged ties between the Trump administration and Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. The billboards, created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP), a nonprofit that describes itself as 'dedicated to reining in Big Tech,' asserted: 'Jensen was in bed with a spy from China.' TOP added, 'Trump was in bed with Jensen.' Meanwhile, Trump is reportedly supporting an effort to bring Huang back as Nvidia's CEO, even though many Republicans have called the move a 'horrible idea.' Breaking his silence on Tuesday, Huang stated he would be 'honored' to return. However, the board indicated that reinstatement is not under consideration while an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. In his statement, Huang emphasized his alignment with American interests, noting: 'I came to the United States 53 years ago.' He described becoming a U.S. citizen as one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of his life, added that Nvidia has been his life's work built alongside colleagues, and concluded by affirming he loves both America and Nvidia. Regarding the espionage allegations, CNN reported that Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was a potential target of Chinese espionage, though the president recently claimed he did not know about it while Huang became part of his inner circle. If Trump was not adequately briefed, CNN said it raises questions about whether the White House acted with 'sufficient urgency' to address what is described as a serious espionage threat. Conversely, if Trump is deflecting, an even 'graver question' may emerge about why he did not act on available information and instead kept Huang close. The article notes these are CNN-reported claims rather than independently verified facts; no specific dates beyond this spring were provided for the alleged briefing timeline.
items.title: Critics Oppose Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia CEO Role Amid Espionage Allegations

items.summary: The article frames Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia as a case study in how human nature undermines cybersecurity. His departure followed reports of multiple affairs, most notably one with Alice Huang, whom U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China; the company stated no secrets were leaked. The author invokes Kevin Mitnick's observation that 'the human factor is truly security's weakest link' to argue that people in powerful positions repeatedly lower their defenses despite having extensive security apparatuses at their disposal. Examples cited include Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni speaking candidly about foreign affairs on a call with Russian pranksters, and former CIA Director David Petraeus giving his biographer access to classified notebooks during an affair. The author attributes these failures partly to how humans are wired to respond to other people: social cues that increase familiarity and intimacy make people feel safer, more trusting, and more willing to divulge information or take risks. Regarding the power of voice, a study conducted with social psychologist Mahdi Roghanizad found participants received about twice as many 'yes' responses when asking for favors by phone compared to email; hearing a person's voice also makes them seem more capable and relatable than reading their written thoughts. On touch, an 1984 study found servers who lightly touched diners receiving change got bigger tips, another classic study found people were 76% more likely to give change when experimenters lightly touched their arm, and a 2010 study found participants took greater financial risks after being given a comforting pat on the shoulder; researchers theorized these touches created familiarity that made people more willing to open their wallets. On face-to-face interaction, Milgram's shock experiment showed nearly two-thirds of participants administered shocks up to the highest setting when an experimenter stood behind them and gave instructions in person, versus only 22.5% when the experimenter left the room and instructed over the phone; a separate study found people were 34 times more likely to say yes to requests made in person than by email, while another study found in-person requests significantly outperformed those made over phone or video call. The author concludes that although cyberattacks and phishing emails pose real threats, some of the biggest risks come from people physically present with you, illustrating a vulnerability even robust cybersecurity measures struggle to guard against.
items.title: Jensen Huang Scandal Illustrates Why Human Nature Is Cybersecurity's Weakest Link

items.summary: During the keynote for its Tuesday Ignite conference, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several enterprise AI updates centered on agentic capabilities. The lead product is Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, "multiplayer" surface for Copilot's agentic features; it is available in Frontier and resembles OpenAI's ChatGPT Space as well as recent Anthropic additions such as Whiteboard and Sheets by merging familiar work tools with an agentic framework. Microsoft also introduced Autopilot, described as a counterpoint agent to Copilot that can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring tasks, and manage projects without waiting for prompts; in a demo it functioned similarly to OpenAI's Dots but oriented toward work, letting employees tag the agent "like a colleague" and assign tasks. Microsoft said Autopilot will autonomously handle meetings and follow-ups, though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves. On trust, Microsoft noted that "Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses," with each instance carrying its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager so IT can block it as needed; sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name for auditability, and it is powered by Work IQ to operate within existing permissions. Employees will soon be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces, also in Frontier. Nadella additionally announced "Today," a command center spanning email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and Teams threads; currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it offers a personalized briefing and an intraday feed of priorities, with Microsoft describing draft edits ready to review, proposed schedule changes, and forgotten follow-ups delivered with context. Home is now generally available as a unified starting point merging Chat and Cowork, mirroring Anthropic's recent consolidation of chat and agentic offerings in the push toward simplification. To address agent costs, which remain high when unsupervised, Microsoft introduced Agent 365 Business Analytics (in Frontier Public) for observability into spending on AI—what is being spent, why, where it pays off, and future cost forecasts—and a demo showed admins spotting spikes in specific agents' costs with suggested human notifications. Microsoft framed this as measuring investment "in work completed, not simply tokens," analyzing tasks, typical human time, and the share Cowork performed to estimate supported hours and value; Agent 365 Cost Management lets IT see AI usage down to the model level, enabling spending policies, limits, proactive alerts, and model availability controls. Anthropic released a similar tool last month focused on maximizing seat efficiency across Teams and Enterprise plans.
items.title: Microsoft Unveils Copilot Workspaces and Agentic Workplace Tools at Ignite 2026

items.summary: On Tuesday, Nvidia held its first earnings call in its 33-year history without cofounder Jensen Huang, who had resigned five days earlier following a scandal involving an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy. After reporting strong third-quarter results, interim CEO Colette Kress—Nvidia's CFO since 2013—took over the call and kept it focused on Nvidia's immediate business concerns rather than its leadership transition. Analysts had wanted to know what the company would say about succession planning after Huang's departure and about the future of Nvidia's role as the company powering the AI race. Most salient information about Huang came from Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board, who said the company does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO—a response to a growing contingent on social media lobbying for his return. Jones noted that executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles is handling the search and that Nvidia is considering both internal and external candidates. He added: "The board is acting deliberately and in the best interest of the company's employees and investors," before stating the company would take no further questions about the circumstances of Jensen's resignation. Kress then took over and focused on the quarterly numbers, which she had run for years but always alongside Huang, who set the company's vision and handled much of its dealmaking with customers and partners. Her main task was to report results and convince investors that Nvidia can operate without its founder. The figures were strong: Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for fiscal third quarter, well above Wall Street's roughly $109 billion forecast, and projected $130 billion for the current quarter—outcomes investors had expected to beat. Kress said Nvidia has seen "explosive" adoption of its latest Vera Rubin computing platform, which includes a Rubin GPU and a Vera CPU, adding: "Our momentum is real." She also affirmed that the company's ambition and passion for innovation would not change.
items.title: Nvidia's first earnings call without Jensen Huang signals business as usual amid leadership transition

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Microsoft has introduced Agent 365 Business Analytics, a tool designed to estimate the business value of AI agents. The product maps labor-market economics onto AI usage data by combining real labor-costing information from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph with data gathered from Agent 365 itself. Microsoft frames this as an attempt to answer how much individual agents, models, and users cost; what business activities AI is performing across more than 6,000 defined use cases; how much human work those activities would ordinarily require; what that work is worth in dollar terms; and whether increasing or reducing AI spending makes business sense. The overall goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced. Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense, treating the task as a hybrid rather than pure software accounting. For example, it may determine how much human effort a task would normally take and price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates; then factor in what fraction of the task was done by humans versus AI along with the estimated value of the AI's contribution; and finally mix in actual AI processing costs across subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support. The resulting hybrid estimate combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and potentially AI savings over human costs. Microsoft notes that these figures are directional estimates rather than measured outcomes, stating: "Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return." This means the estimated value may not align with real-world experience or expenses, since AI work might have been assigned because there was AI available to do it rather than because the AI was saving company labor costs. The author observes that this is notable given Microsoft's association with PowerPoint and warns that dashboards could look impressive while being irrelevant to actual results; however, the product is not considered useless, requiring disciplined interpretation of its outputs as one source of possible truth rather than absolute truth. Beyond value estimation, Microsoft positions Agent 365 and related offerings to help organizations monitor AI agents from multiple vendors, manage their identities, permissions, and security, track and limit AI spending, evaluate whether agents deliver value, and decide which systems deserve additional investment. This approach means the company does not necessarily need to provide the underlying AI model or even apps and SaaS capabilities, integrating instead with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others; if it can manage organizational "plumbing," control costs, and serve as an HR operation for the AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of enterprise operations. The article is written by David Gewirtz, who directs readers to his social media channels across Twitter/X, Facebook, Instagram, Bluesky, and YouTube.
items.title: Microsoft's Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates AI value using labor-market economics
